import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Prepare the data
csv_data = """amount,is_fraud,transaction_type,hour_of_day
115.02,0,refund,22
44.37,0,payment,5
144.25,0,transfer,21
536.22,0,payment,17
38.43,0,payment,5
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a professional and visually appealing style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create the figure and axes for the plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 7))

# Create a scatter plot to show the relationship between amount, hour, and type
# Using hue and style for transaction_type provides clear differentiation
# Size is linked to amount to emphasize larger transactions
scatter_plot = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='hour_of_day',
    y='amount',
    hue='transaction_type',
    style='transaction_type',
    size='amount',
    sizes=(100, 500),  # Range of marker sizes
    alpha=0.85,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1.2,
    ax=ax
)

# Set a clear and descriptive title and labels
ax.set_title('Transaction Analysis: Amount by Hour and Type', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Hour of Day (24h format)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Transaction Amount ($)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Customize ticks for better readability
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${x:,.0f}'))

# Set x-axis limits to represent a full day for better context
ax.set_xlim(-1, 24)
ax.set_xticks(range(0, 25, 2))

# Enhance the legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Separate legends for type and size for clarity
type_legend_labels = df['transaction_type'].unique()
type_legend_handles = handles[1:len(type_legend_labels)+1]

legend1 = ax.legend(
    type_legend_handles,
    type_legend_labels,
    title='Transaction Type',
    title_fontsize='13',
    fontsize='11',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.
)
ax.add_artist(legend1) # Add the first legend back to the plot

# Create the second legend for size
size_legend_labels = [h.get_label() for h in handles[len(type_legend_labels)+2:]]
size_legend_handles = handles[len(type_legend_labels)+2:]

legend2 = ax.legend(
    size_legend_handles,
    size_legend_labels,
    title='Amount',
    title_fontsize='13',
    fontsize='11',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 0.6),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.
)


# Use a tight layout to ensure all elements fit, adjusting for the external legend
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1])

# Save the generated visualization to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

# Close the plot to free up memory
plt.close(fig)
